prerequisites: Secondary school mathematics knowledge: First and second-degree algebraic equations, systems of linear equations, inequalities, powers and logarithms, trigonometric functions, use of graphs and percentages, derivatives and integrals.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of the basics for understanding chemical phenomena important in technologies, and, in particular, those related to the interactions between human activity and the environment, to be able to evaluate the effects produced by the use of technologies and to know how to intervene in the safeguarding of environmental conditions and materials.

syllabus_topics: Enthalpy and its use in chemistry
Effects of pressure, concentration and temperature
Slightly soluble salts and solubility product
Acids and bases and their strength
Thermodynamics of chemical energy transformation into electrical energy: Nernst equation
Quantum mechanics: wave-particle dualism and uncertainty principle
Quantization and properties of wave functions
Ionic, molecular, metallic solids and their properties
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of a 90-minute written test with 20 numerical questions and theoretical questions. Each correct answer is awarded 1.5 points for a total of 30 points, with no penalties for wrong answers. The written test is followed by an oral test, primarily a discussion of the written test and questions on atomic structure, the periodic table, and chemical bonding. During the written test, books, computers, and notes may be consulted.
bibliography: David W. Oxtoby, H. P. Gillis & Laurie J. Butler, Chimica Moderna, EdiSES, Napoli
degree: Corso di laurea in Ingegneria meccanica (L-9)
